portfolio construction decisions can
largely be replicated by AI with a
neural network correctly forecasting
approximately 71%
of quarterly buy, sell, or hold
decisions.
The algorithm was calibrated using
rolling 5-year samples from 1990 through
2023, incorporating variables such as
fund size, investor flows, equity
attributes, and macroeconomic
conditions, enabling it to project the
bulk of portfolio reallocations.
Notably,
the roughly 29% of trades the system
could not predict were on average more
tightly linked to excess returns,
indicating that departures from
systematic observable patterns are
responsible for the majority of alpha
generation.
The findings suggest machines have
internalized much of the asset
management industry's standard operating
framework, particularly responses to
flows, price action, and peer
positioning, while remaining less
effective at modeling the minority of
discretionary decisions that deviate
from that template.

unsystematic nature of alpha generation
